name: Loki
description: Grafana Loki reads over its HTTP query API: known label names and their values, a LogQL range query, and the log streams matching a label selector. Read-only; no push/ingest endpoint is wired here. It is unauthenticated by default (base_url is the only credential); put it behind a reverse proxy or Grafana's own auth for exposure beyond a trusted LAN.

tools.name: labels
tools.description: List every log label name known to this Loki instance

start.description: Optional start timestamp to bound the lookup

end.description: Optional end timestamp to bound the lookup

tools.name: label_values
tools.description: List the values a given log label takes across streams (e.g. job, namespace)

label.description: Label name to list values for, e.g. job or namespace

tools.name: query_range
tools.description: Run a LogQL query over a time range and return the matching log streams and entries

start.description: Range start, a Unix timestamp in nanoseconds

end.description: Range end, a Unix timestamp in nanoseconds

limit.description: Max number of entries to return

tools.name: series
tools.description: List the log streams (label sets) matching one or more stream selectors

start.description: Optional start timestamp to bound the lookup

end.description: Optional end timestamp to bound the lookup

needs_review: AUTH IS none BY DESIGN: Loki ships with no authentication of its own on the query HTTP API (auth_enabled defaults true only in multi-tenant mode with an X-Scope-OrgID header, not a credential), so base_url is the only credential and auth.type is 'none'. Fronting Loki with a reverse proxy or Grafana's auth is a deployment concern, not a spec one.
READ-ONLY: all four tools are GET, write:false. Loki's ingest surface (/loki/api/v1/push) is not modelled here.
labels and label_values return {"status":"success"} with the data key omitted or empty on a fresh instance with no ingested logs; that is a valid 200 proof of the endpoint, not a failure.

query_range and series probe a FIXED nanosecond window (2020-09-13) with a catch-all selector {job=~".+"}; on a fresh instance the honest expected result is a 200 success envelope with an empty result/data array, proving routing and the envelope shape, not real log content.

LIVE-PROOF CONTRACT: labels takes no required input (_probe {}); label_values pins job; query_range and series pin the fixed window/selector above. Proven against docker grafana/loki:3.1.1, then destroyed.
